create.title: Fixed-lift primitive residue support-mask Fourier kernel
create.statement_tex: Fix one primitive top-shell outer ray (a,b), one physical increment p, put m=a+p, and set n=aq-bp. After physical primitive support is established, let M be the odd part of |m|. The stripped M1 support-character mask w_1(q)=chi_4(b+q) 1_((M,b+q)=1) has minimal q-period 4 rad(M), admits completion modulus 4M, and has normalized DFT exp(kb/(4M)) G_(4,M)(k)c_M(k)/(4M). The mod-four Gauss factor vanishes for even k and has magnitude 2 for odd k, so the zero coefficient vanishes while the k=M,3M coefficients have magnitude phi(M)/(2M) and pull back to the two determinant quarter frequencies. For active odd m, the stripped M2 mask w_2(q)=epsilon_sgn chi_4(|m|)1_((|m|,b+q)=1) has minimal period rad(|m|), admits completion modulus |m|, and has DFT epsilon_sgn chi_4(|m|) exp(kb/|m|)c_|m|(k)/|m|; its fixed-p q-arithmetic k=0 coefficient is epsilon_sgn chi_4(|m|)phi(|m|)/|m| and is generically nonzero. Both normalized Fourier l1 costs are divisor-sized. These are support-mask identities, not a factorization of rho-dependent physical profiles or a signed estimate, and Fourier k=0 is not the determinant point n=0.

create.title: Variable-modulus residue interlacing and cross-ray capacity obstruction
create.statement_tex: On the W=Y^(7/16), D=Y^(1/2), L=Y^(1/6) top shell, the complete p-interlaced physical determinant weight has no proved common 4|a|-periodic arithmetic factor times a target-cost BV envelope. Physical primitivity introduces m=a+p: post-reassembly M1 divisor support atoms have determinant period |a|lcm(4,rho), M2 atoms have |a|rho, and hiding primitivity in the envelope gives linear variation. The bare Mobius incidence identity does not factor rho-dependent profiles, stars, or owners. Natural p-order profiles can incur O(L) determinant-order switches, erasing a full L Abel gain. The exact n>0 same-denominator M1 and M2 packets have length D/W and refute character-forced per-ray vanishing, but their centres and physical amplitudes do not give a family lower bound. One packet has capacity Y^(30/48+o(1)); the full cell cover recovers Y^(35/48+o(1)) only as worst-case capacity. Fixed-lift arithmetic is Gauss-times-Ramanujan, not a growing quadratic-Gauss or Salie sum. Even ideal one-term-per-ray collapse reaches only Y^(27/48)=Y^(9/16), so strict global improvement requires an actual cross-ray power and the Y^(1/2) determinant target requires a further Y^(-1/16). This is a method and coefficient-interface obstruction, not a lower bound for the actual family.
